summary: Regression testing of the rewritten /app/frontend/src/components/magic/Stack.jsx (drag+tap photo-stack gallery on /products/{slug}). Verified library wiring (framer-motion motion.div + drag + onDragEnd + onTap + whileDrag + spring transition + touchAction:none + Math.sin(i*13.37) deterministic rotation are ALL present in the file). E2E-tested on /products/zzdrag-stacktest-5ac476 with 3 picsum images. Findings: TAP works correctly (single fire, cycles by 1 per tap). DRAG on DESKTOP viewport (1920x1080) INCORRECTLY cycles by TWO positions per gesture — onDragEnd AND onTap are both firing on release, causing sendToBack() to fire twice. DRAG on MOBILE viewport (390x844) shifts by ONE (correct). Random rotation active on all 3 cards, touchAction:none honored, whileDrag scale/zIndex works, spring return visible in screenshots. This is a business-logic bug in the Stack.jsx tap/drag coordination.

ui_bugs.issue: Desktop drag fires sendToBack TWICE per gesture. Root cause: framer-motion's onTap handler fires AFTER onDragEnd on desktop mouse drags (both handlers run), so the top card cycles by 2 positions instead of 1. Empirical reproduction with a fresh page: order was [1,2,3]; a single mouse drag (200px right, 25 steps @20ms) produced order [3,1,2] (2-step cycle), and a second drag returned it to [1,2,3]. Round-trip after 3 drags fails: initial=seed-1, after_drag3=seed-3 (should be seed-1). Two-drag round-trip DOES work only because a 2-cycle shift ×3 = 6 = 0 mod 3 by coincidence… wait actually observed after_drag3=seed-3 which is NOT the initial → round-trip broken.

In the combined test (3 drags + 1 tap on same page), the TAP appeared to not cycle. However in an ISOLATED fresh-page tap test, tap correctly cycled by 1 with no double-fire. Cause is likely related to residual pointer/pan state left by the previous drag — not a tap bug per se, but a symptom of the same drag/tap coordination issue.

issues: Rotation values measured in computed transform are much smaller than the code's stated ±5° range (observed ~-0.33°, +0.30°, +0.10° at rest). The requested-random-rotation formula ((sin(i*13.37) - floor) - 0.5)*10 gives roughly -5, +4.7, -4.1 for i=0,1,2 but framer-motion's `animate={{rotate: baseRot}}` seems to be interpolating to a much smaller final value. Visually the rotation is present (see screenshots) — cards ARE tilted a few degrees. This may be either (a) framer normalising through the spring, or (b) the initial vs final animate state mismatch. Cosmetic, does not affect drag/tap behavior.

action_items: HIGH — Fix double-fire in Stack.jsx: framer-motion's onTap is firing in addition to onDragEnd on desktop drags. Suggested fix: track a `didDragRef = useRef(false)` — set true in `onDragStart`, then in `onTap` bail early if `didDragRef.current` and reset it. Also reset in `onDragEnd` after a short microtask/timeout so a subsequent tap on the same top card still fires. Example patch inside the motion.div: `onDragStart={() => (didDragRef.current = true)}` and `onTap={() => { if (didDragRef.current) { didDragRef.current = false; return; } if (isTop && sendToBackOnClick) sendToBack(); }}`. Alternative: remove `onTap` and rely solely on onDragEnd + a raw onClick with a tiny movement guard.
MEDIUM — Verify the fix restores the round-trip invariant: with N images and N drags, top card must equal the initial image (currently fails on desktop).

LOW — Investigate why the resting `rotate` is 0.1-0.3° instead of the ±5° computed by Math.sin(i*13.37). Screenshots do show visible tilt (~3-5°) so the value at some point is correct; the resting matrix may be sampled mid-transition or overridden.
critical_code_review_comments: Stack.jsx: All required library wiring is present — `import { motion } from 'framer-motion'` (L2), `drag={isTop}` (L60), `onDragEnd` (L64), `onTap` (L72), `whileDrag` (L84), `transition={{type:'spring',...}}` (L82), `touchAction:'none'` (L87), `Math.sin(i*13.37)` (L34). The file passes the 'library correctly wired' check.

Stack.jsx L60-75: The onTap handler unconditionally calls sendToBack when isTop && sendToBackOnClick, without checking whether a drag just ended. Framer-motion@11.18 does not always suppress onTap after a completed drag gesture on desktop mouse events — this is the source of the double-fire. Add a drag-flag guard.

Stack.jsx L63: `dragConstraints={{left:0,right:0,top:0,bottom:0}}` combined with `dragMomentum:false` and `dragElastic:0.7` means the card visually only stretches a bit and spring-returns. This is fine for the 'toss' feel but keeps the pointer over the card at release, which may increase the chance of onTap also being fired. Consider removing dragElastic (or setting to 0) so drag feels like a real toss, and framer's Pan gesture more cleanly wins over Press.

ProductDetail.jsx L93-96: correctly renders Stack only when images.length >= 3. Hint text 'Geser atau tap kartu untuk foto berikutnya' present and visible. Absolute picsum URLs pass through getFileUrl unchanged (verified in screenshots — images loaded fine).
Positive: touchAction:'none' is honored on all cards (verified via getComputedStyle). draggable={false} on prevents native image-drag interference. Deterministic rotation avoids per-render jitter.

rca of the issue: Root cause: In framer-motion@11.18, when the user drags a motion.div that has BOTH `drag` and `onTap` set, on mouse (desktop) pointer up the library invokes onDragEnd AND ALSO onTap (Press gesture is not always cancelled by Pan on desktop mouse). Because Stack.jsx wires both handlers to call sendToBack() unconditionally, each desktop drag cycles the stack by 2. Mobile (pointerType=touch) does not exhibit this because the touch pan gesture cleanly cancels the tap. Reproduction: single mouse drag of 200px right on top card shifts stack order by 2 positions instead of 1. Mitigation: introduce a `useRef` flag (e.g., didDragRef) set true in onDragStart, checked-and-cleared in onTap so tap is skipped when a drag just happened. This is a ~4-line change in Stack.jsx.
